latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Active EBV replication in oropharyngeal epithelium and B lymphocytes (or CMV in monocytes/endothelium) driving antigen load; underlies viremia, viral shedding, and downstream immune response
EBV-infected B cells proliferate and secrete polyclonal Ig (heterophile antibodies, autoantibodies, cold agglutinins); generates the antibody-mediated complications and the Paul-Bunnell response

Massive oligoclonal CD8+ cytotoxic T-cell response targeting EBV-infected B cells (or CMV-infected cells); produces Downey-type atypical lymphocytes and causes most clinical manifestations of the syndrome
EBV replication in oropharyngeal epithelium plus reactive lymphoid expansion in Waldeyer's ring producing exudative pharyngitis, tonsillar enlargement, and (rarely) airway compromise

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Generalized reticuloendothelial / lymph node / splenic lymphoid expansion
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: T- and B-cell hyperplasia in lymph nodes and splenic white/red pulp; mechanistic substrate of generalized lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, and splenic capsular fragility

Cytotoxic T-cell-mediated injury of EBV/CMV-infected hepatocytes and Kupffer cells producing transaminitis (ALT/AST elevation in 80-90% of cases), mild cholestasis, and hepatomegaly; usually self-limited but rarely fulminant
IL-6/IFN-gamma-driven systemic acute-phase response generating fever, malaise, and modest CRP/ferritin elevation; less intense than bacterial sepsis or HLH
Polyclonal autoantibody and immune-complex production driving cold-agglutinin AIHA, immune thrombocytopenia, and (rarely) neutropenia/aplastic anemia during or after acute mono

Pre-clinical activation of macrophages by sustained IFN-gamma/IL-18 signaling; in a small minority of cases (especially XLP, primary HLH, or immunocompromised hosts) progresses to overt EBV-driven HLH/MAS

Prolonged fatigue, exercise intolerance, and somnolence persisting for weeks to months after acute infection clears; mechanism likely involves sustained low-grade cytokine signaling and CNS/HPA effects

mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Plasma EBV DNA copies reflect lytic replication burden

mechanism_edges.conditionality: applies when etiology is CMV (heterophile-negative mono)
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Plasma CMV DNA reflects replication; antigenemia/PCR positivity in ~60-90% of acute CMV mono
EBV directly infects B cells via CD21, driving polyclonal proliferation and Ig secretion
Antigen presentation by infected B cells triggers massive CD8+ cytotoxic T-cell expansion which dominates the clinical phase
Lytic EBV replication in oropharyngeal epithelium and tonsillar B cells drives tonsillar hyperplasia and exudate

mechanism_edges.conditionality: EBV only; CMV mono is heterophile-negative
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Polyclonal B-cell activation produces Paul-Bunnell heterophile antibodies (sheep/horse RBC agglutinins); positive in ~85% of EBV cases by week 2-3, ~25% false-negative rate in week 1, near-universal negative in CMV/HHV6/HIV/Toxoplasma mono and in young children
Anti-VCA IgM rises during acute phase and disappears by 1-3 months; most specific marker of acute primary EBV infection
VCA-IgG appears acutely and persists for life; without VCA-IgM or with positive EBNA-IgG indicates past infection

mechanism_edges.conditionality: EBV etiology; absent during acute phase by definition
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: EBNA-IgG seroconverts 6-12 weeks after onset; presence during acute illness rules out primary EBV (suggests reactivation or other etiology)
Polyclonal autoantibody production includes cold-agglutinin anti-i (AIHA) and antiplatelet antibodies (ITP)
Activated CD8+ T cells appear as Downey-type atypical (large, basophilic, indented nucleus) lymphocytes; >10% is characteristic, >20-30% is highly suggestive
Absolute and relative lymphocytosis (>50% of WBC, often with absolute count 4.5-15 x10^9/L) is the hematologic hallmark
Total WBC typically 12-25 x10^9/L during peak; lymphocyte-predominant (contrasts with bacterial pharyngitis where WBC is neutrophil-predominant)
CD8+ T cells attack EBV-infected hepatocytes/Kupffer cells; CMV similarly causes T-cell-mediated hepatitis (often more prominent than in EBV)
Lymph node and splenic T-cell infiltration produce generalized lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly
IFN-gamma from activated CTLs primes macrophages; in genetically susceptible hosts (XLP, perforin defects) drives EBV-HLH
ALT elevation in 80-90% of cases; typically 2-5x ULN, occasionally >10x ULN; CMV mono often shows higher transaminitis than EBV
AST rises in parallel with ALT; usually mild-moderate
Mild ALP elevation common; reflects mixed hepatocellular/cholestatic pattern
Mild bilirubin elevation in ~25-45%; clinical jaundice in 5-10%
LDH elevation reflects both hepatocellular injury and lymphoproliferation
Tender hepatomegaly in 10-20% of cases

mechanism_edges.conditionality: rare; greatly increased in XLP, immunocompromised, primary HLH
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Fulminant hepatic failure is rare (<1%) but classic in X-linked lymphoproliferative disorder and immunocompromised hosts
Severe exudative pharyngitis is the cardinal early symptom in EBV mono
Whitish-grey exudate with kissing tonsils in 50-90% of EBV mono; often more confluent than streptococcal pharyngitis
Petechiae at the junction of hard and soft palate present in ~25-50%; relatively specific finding

mechanism_edges.conditionality: occurs in <1-5% of cases with massive tonsillar enlargement
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Kissing tonsils with airway compromise is a classic indication for systemic corticosteroids
Tender symmetric posterior cervical lymphadenopathy is classic; generalized adenopathy with axillary and inguinal involvement helps distinguish from streptococcal pharyngitis
Palpable splenomegaly in ~50%; sonographic splenomegaly even more common; peaks in week 2-3

mechanism_edges.conditionality: occurs in 0.1-0.5% of cases; ~half spontaneous, half traumatic; highest risk weeks 2-3
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Splenic capsule fragility from lymphoid expansion; basis for activity restriction (no contact sports) for at least 3-4 weeks from symptom onset
Hoagland sign: bilateral upper eyelid edema in ~25-30% during early illness; relatively specific
Fever 38-40°C in nearly all symptomatic cases; typically 7-14 days, occasionally longer in CMV mono
Profound fatigue is dominant symptom; often the last to resolve
Myalgias and headache are common prodromal/early features
Frontal headache is a frequent prodromal symptom
CRP modestly elevated (typically 10-80 mg/L); much lower than in bacterial pharyngitis with similar symptoms when severe
Mild-moderate ferritin elevation; markedly elevated ferritin (>10,000 ng/mL) should prompt workup for EBV-HLH
Mild thrombocytopenia in ~25-50% (typically 100-150 x10^9/L); severe ITP in ~1%

mechanism_edges.conditionality: AIHA in ~1-3%; cold agglutinin (anti-i specificity) common subclinically
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Cold-agglutinin AIHA can produce moderate-to-severe hemolytic anemia, occasionally requiring corticosteroids
Mild neutropenia in 50-80% during the lymphocytosis phase; usually self-limited
DAT positive (typically C3d only, IgG-negative) reflects cold-agglutinin pattern

mechanism_edges.conditionality: rare in immunocompetent hosts; greatly increased in XLP, primary HLH, immunocompromised
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: EBV is the most common viral trigger of secondary HLH; suspect with persistent fever, marked ferritin >10000, cytopenias, splenomegaly, hypofibrinogenemia, hypertriglyceridemia
Fatigue persists 2-6 months in 10-20% of patients; small subset develops post-infectious chronic fatigue syndrome

mechanism_edges.conditionality: spontaneous rash in 5-15%; aminopenicillin-induced rash in ~80-95% if amoxicillin/ampicillin is given
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Spontaneous maculopapular rash uncommon; aminopenicillin exposure during acute mono produces a near-universal pruritic morbilliform rash via transient drug-specific IgM/immune complex mechanism (not type I allergy)
Neurologic complications include encephalitis, Bell's palsy, Guillain-Barré syndrome, transverse myelitis, cerebellitis, optic neuritis (Alice in Wonderland syndrome especially in children)

axes.shape_free_text: Onset over 1-3 days, peaks 38.5-40°C, plateau 7-14 days then gradual defervescence; CMV mono fever often more prolonged (up to 3-4 weeks)
Severe pharyngitis emerging early, peaks days 5-10, resolves over 1-2 weeks
Whitish-grey confluent exudate on enlarged tonsils peaking days 5-10
Transient petechiae at hard-soft palate junction in ~25-50% during week 1-2
Bilateral upper eyelid edema (Hoagland sign) early in course in ~25%
Tender symmetric posterior cervical lymphadenopathy plus generalized (axillary, inguinal, epitrochlear); peaks week 2, resolves over 4-6 weeks
Palpable in ~50%, sonographic in ~75%; peaks week 2-3; persists 4-6 weeks
Tender hepatomegaly in 10-20%; usually mild
Profound fatigue from prodrome; peaks weeks 2-3; gradual resolution over 4-12 weeks; persistent in 10-20% beyond 3 months
Myalgia common in prodrome and early phase
Frontal headache in 50-70% during prodrome and early acute phase
Spontaneous maculopapular rash in 5-15%; near-universal pruritic morbilliform rash if amoxicillin/ampicillin is administered (peaks days 7-10 after drug exposure)
Significant pruritus accompanies aminopenicillin rash and is occasionally seen with cholestatic mono
Rare (<1-5%): encephalitis, GBS, Bell's palsy, transverse myelitis, optic neuritis; usually weeks 2-4
Mild leukocytosis 12-25 x10^9/L by week 2; lymphocyte-predominant
Absolute lymphocytosis (often >4.5, may reach 15) with >50% lymphocytes by week 2
Downey-type atypical lymphocytes >0.10 (often 0.20-0.40) of WBC differential by week 2; gradual normalization over 4-6 weeks
Mild neutropenia common; recovers as lymphocytosis resolves
Mild thrombocytopenia (100-150) common; severe ITP rare
Usually normal; mild AIHA-related drop in subset, severe AIHA rare
Elevation in 80-90%; typically 2-5x ULN, occasionally >10x ULN; CMV often higher than EBV; peak week 2-3, normalizes 4-8 weeks
Parallel to ALT; normalizes slightly earlier
Mildly elevated in many cases (1-2x ULN)
Mild elevation in ~25-45%; clinical jaundice in 5-10%
Elevated 1.5-3x ULN reflecting both hepatocellular injury and lymphoproliferation
Modest elevation, usually 10-80 mg/L; helps distinguish from bacterial sepsis (typically >150)
Typically low (<0.5) in viral mono; supports viral over bacterial etiology
Mild-moderate elevation (300-2000); marked elevation (>10000) suggests progression to EBV-HLH
Plasma EBV DNA detectable in acute primary EBV; peaks 10^3-10^5 copies/mL during weeks 2-4; declines but may remain low-positive for months in B-cell compartment
CMV DNA detectable in heterophile-negative mono of CMV etiology; usually 10^2-10^4 copies/mL
Paul-Bunnell/Monospot positive in ~85% of EBV mono by week 2-3; ~25% false-negative in week 1; near-universal negative in CMV/HHV6/HIV/Toxoplasma mono and in young children (<4 years)
Anti-VCA IgM rises early, peaks weeks 2-4, becomes undetectable by 1-3 months; specific marker of acute primary EBV
VCA-IgG rises during acute illness and persists for life
EBNA-IgG seroconverts 6-12 weeks after symptom onset; absence during acute phase confirms primary infection; presence rules it out
CMV IgM positive in acute CMV mono; can persist months and cross-react in EBV; interpret with avidity testing if uncertain
Often C3d-positive (cold-agglutinin pattern, anti-i specificity); evident if AIHA
Rare (lifetime risk per case 0.1-0.5%); peaks weeks 2-3; about half spontaneous, half traumatic; basis for activity restriction
Rare (<1-5%); peaks during maximal tonsillar swelling weeks 1-2; classic indication for systemic corticosteroids
Very rare in immunocompetent (<0.1%); markedly elevated in XLP, primary HLH, immunocompromised
Rare overall; EBV is the most common viral trigger of secondary HLH; risk concentrated in genetically predisposed and immunocompromised hosts
Long-term latent risk after primary EBV infection (Hodgkin lymphoma, Burkitt, post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder, NPC); not a feature of acute illness
Persistent fatigue / chronic fatigue syndrome activity at month 1-6 after acute illness; ~10-20% have persistent fatigue at 6 months
Overall mortality very low (<0.1%) in immunocompetent hosts; concentrated in fulminant hepatitis, splenic rupture, EBV-HLH, airway obstruction; markedly higher in XLP, primary HLH, post-transplant

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Both reflect the same underlying CD8+ T-cell expansion; atypical lymphocyte fraction and absolute lymphocyte count rise together
AST and ALT rise together in viral hepatitis; ratio typically near 1 or AST<ALT
Hepatomegaly tends to accompany higher transaminitis but correlation is loose
Splenic rupture risk is concentrated in patients with palpable splenomegaly during weeks 2-3
Massive ('kissing') tonsils are the proximal cause of airway compromise
Ferritin >10,000 ng/mL strongly raises probability of EBV-HLH; >3,000 warrants close monitoring with full HLH-2004 workup
Persistently high or rising plasma EBV DNA correlates with progression to EBV-HLH and underlying lymphoma risk
Both are markers of active polyclonal/EBV-specific B-cell response; concordant when EBV is the etiology
Both driven by IL-6/IFN-gamma acute-phase signaling
Mild thrombocytopenia partly reflects splenic sequestration plus immune mechanism

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Reduce dose or avoid in significant hepatitis to minimize hepatotoxic risk

failure_modes: inadequate symptom control with severe pharyngitis

side_effects.interpretation: minor risk at therapeutic doses; relevant if hepatitis is prominent

treatments.context_specific_role: First-line antipyretic/analgesic for fever, pharyngitis, headache, myalgia

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Avoid in significant thrombocytopenia or active bleeding

side_effects.interpretation: antiplatelet effect; mild concern in mono-related thrombocytopenia

treatments.context_specific_role: Adjunct for pharyngitis-related pain and fever

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Impending airway compromise from massive tonsillar enlargement is the classic indication
Severe AIHA from cold agglutinins may benefit
Component of HLH-94/2004 protocol if EBV-HLH evolves
Avoid empirical steroids if lymphoma is on differential without diagnostic biopsy first

failure_modes: use in uncomplicated mono is NOT recommended (no benefit on duration of illness, may prolong viral shedding)

side_effects.interpretation: may transiently increase viral load and shedding

treatments.context_specific_role: Reserved for impending airway obstruction, severe AIHA/ITP, fulminant hepatitis, neurologic complications, EBV-HLH progression; not for routine mono

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Reduces oropharyngeal viral shedding but does NOT improve clinical course in immunocompetent mono; not recommended routinely

failure_modes: no clinical benefit in uncomplicated immunocompetent mono
treatments.context_specific_role: Considered for severe complications (oral hairy leukoplakia in HIV, severe EBV in immunocompromised, EBV encephalitis in select cases); not routine

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Used for severe organ-involving CMV (CMV pneumonitis, colitis, retinitis) typically in immunocompromised; NOT routine for CMV mononucleosis in immunocompetent

treatments.context_specific_role: CMV mono is self-limited in immunocompetent; ganciclovir reserved for severe/organ-invasive CMV in immunocompromised hosts

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: EBV-HLH and post-transplant EBV-PTLD: rituximab depletes EBV-infected B-cell reservoir

side_effects.interpretation: B-cell depletion increases bacterial/viral infection risk for months
screen and treat HBV before use

treatments.context_specific_role: Reserved for EBV-HLH, EBV-PTLD, severe EBV-driven lymphoproliferation in immunocompromised; not routine mono

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Cornerstone of HLH-94/2004 protocol; selectively eliminates activated cytotoxic T cells driving EBV-HLH

treatments.context_specific_role: Specific to EBV-HLH per HLH-2004 (combined with dexamethasone +/- cyclosporine, with rituximab adjunct)

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Adjunct in immune-mediated neurologic complications (GBS, encephalitis)

treatments.context_specific_role: Severe ITP, AIHA, GBS, encephalitis complications

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Aminopenicillins precipitate near-universal pruritic morbilliform rash in EBV mono (~80-95%); avoid empirically when mono is on the differential for pharyngitis

treatments.context_specific_role: Listed because frequently misprescribed as empirical pharyngitis treatment before mono is recognized; should NOT be given when mono is suspected

young_adult_15_to_25_years.trajectory_modulation: peak symptomatic incidence; classic clinical syndrome with severe pharyngitis, splenomegaly, and atypical lymphocytosis

child_under_5_years.trajectory_modulation: often mild/atypical; heterophile antibody frequently negative, requiring EBV-specific serology

older_adult_over_40.trajectory_modulation: more prominent hepatitis and prolonged fever; lower frequency of pharyngitis and lymphadenopathy; CMV etiology relatively more common

recent_new_partner_or_kissing_contact.trajectory_modulation: saliva is the dominant transmission route ('kissing disease'); incubation 4-7 weeks

seronegative.trajectory_modulation: primary infection produces full clinical syndrome

seropositive_past_infection.trajectory_modulation: primary EBV mono cannot recur; alternative etiologies (CMV/HHV6/HIV/Toxoplasma) must be considered for mono-like illness

hiv_acute_seroconversion.trajectory_modulation: acute HIV is a leading cause of heterophile-negative mono-like illness; mandatory to test if heterophile-negative

post_transplant_or_chemotherapy.trajectory_modulation: high risk of EBV-PTLD and CMV organ disease; lower threshold for antiviral and rituximab

primary_immunodeficiency_xlp.trajectory_modulation: X-linked lymphoproliferative disease (SH2D1A/XIAP): fulminant fatal mono with hepatic necrosis, HLH, hypogammaglobulinemia, lymphoma; consider in any male with severe/fatal EBV

hla_class_I_certain_alleles.trajectory_modulation: HLA-A*01 increases severity; HLA-A*02 protective; modest effect

developed_country_temperate.trajectory_modulation: delayed primary infection into adolescence/young adulthood produces classic mono syndrome

developing_country_or_low_socioeconomic.trajectory_modulation: early childhood primary infection often subclinical; mono-like presentation rarer

supportive_care: Acetaminophen or NSAIDs for fever, pharyngitis, myalgia (caution NSAIDs in thrombocytopenia)
Saltwater gargles or topical anesthetics for pharyngitis
Activity restriction: avoid contact sports, weight-lifting, and vigorous exertion for at least 3-4 weeks from symptom onset (longer if splenomegaly persists on imaging) to reduce splenic rupture risk

Avoid empirical aminopenicillins (amoxicillin/ampicillin) when mono is on the differential due to drug-induced morbilliform rash; if the patient is mistakenly told they are 'penicillin-allergic' from this rash, document that this is not true IgE-mediated allergy
Avoid alcohol and other hepatotoxins until transaminitis resolves
Counseling on expected course: fever 1-2 weeks, pharyngitis 1-2 weeks, fatigue 4-12 weeks, full recovery in most by 2-3 months
Workup heterophile-negative mono with EBV-specific serology, CMV serology/PCR, HIV RNA/Ag/Ab (acute HIV), Toxoplasma serology, HHV-6
Monitor CBC and LFTs serially during acute illness; rising ferritin/falling fibrinogen/persistent fever warrants HLH-2004 workup
Imaging (ultrasound or CT) for splenic size if abdominal pain or pre-return-to-sport assessment
Hospital admission and corticosteroid trial for impending airway obstruction; ENT consultation for severe tonsillar swelling
Hematology consultation for severe AIHA, ITP, or aplastic anemia features
Hepatology consultation for fulminant hepatitis (rare); evaluate for XLP in young male with severe/fatal EBV
